items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: another old friend of mine, Wild Bill Moore, appeared in town with Christine Chapman... So it was nice to see Wild Bill again.

ctx.x: And this particular night, when they played in Lakeland, Florida, they had only been together four days. And Charlie Parker was sitting on the book. He had memorized the book! [LAUGHS] Yeah...! He was just sitting there staring out in space and playing everything, playing all the lead, everything, you know. It was just fantastic.

So in the meantime, I am still working over at Wat Sanders' Blue Room. And another old friend of mine, Wild Bill Moore, appeared in town with Christine Chapman, the lady...a fine boogie-woogie pianist. She had a big hit at the time called "Naptown Boogie" -- she was out of Indianapolis. So it was nice to see Wild Bill again.

So I'm still doing my trip, and Ernie Fields' Orchestra came to town. And some of the guys came down to the Blue Room and heard me play. They would come in every night. They must have been around there four or five days, and they'd come in and they'd listen to me play. So they went back and really vouched for me to join the band, you know, with Ernie Fields -- talked to Ernie about me. So they got him to come down and hear me. So he gave me a talking...
